newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn expelled U.S. diplomat for spying - Spiegel.
newsitem.headline: Bonn expelled U.S. diplomat for spying - Spiegel.

text.p: Germany has expelled a U.S. diplomat for spying, the magazine Spiegel said on Saturday, adding that the incident between the two close allies was unprecedented.

In a report released ahead of publication Monday, Spiegel said the diplomat had been caught trying to recruit senior officials from Bonn's Economics Ministry and to obtain information on what it called "high-tech projects."
He had been uncovered by Germany's Office for the Protection of the Constitution (BfV), it said, but neither officials there nor at the U.S. embassy in Bonn were available for comment.

Spiegel said that because of the good relations between the two NATO allies, the affair was discreetly settled by the U.S. and German intelligence agencies without a formal summons for the U.S. ambassador and without declaring the man persona non grata.
A spokeswoman for the U.S. State Department declined comment on the report. "If this report is true, the State Department has a policy that we do not comment on intelligence matters."
The Central Intelligence Agency was not immediately available for comment.

Spiegel said the U.S. diplomat had left Germany, citing Chancellor Helmut Kohl's security coordinator Bernd Schmidbauer and that Bonn had asked Washington to "drastically reduce" the number of CIA officials it had operating in Germany.
A Chancellery spokesman declined comment on the report.
